images.title: Three steps through fractions
images.purpose: Recap the topic's method: write each decimal as a fraction, multiply, then write the product back as a decimal.
images.composition: Four boxes in one horizontal row joined by three arrows, with a short step name over each arrow; white space above and below.
exact_structure: Exactly 4 rounded boxes in one row, left to right, joined by exactly 3 grey #6B7280 arrows pointing right.
Above arrow 1 the small grey text "as fractions", above arrow 2 "multiply", above arrow 3 "as a decimal".
rejection: more or fewer than 4 boxes or 3 arrows
the step names placed over the wrong arrows
images.takeaway: To multiply decimals, go through fractions: 1.2 × 0.3 = 12/10 × 3/10 = 36/100 = 0.36.
images.description: Four boxes joined by arrows: 1.2 × 0.3, then 12/10 × 3/10, then 36/100, then 0.36, with the steps as fractions, multiply and as a decimal.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept as a compact recap of the fraction method before the questions.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the arrows left to right and name each step before trying a question.

image_decisions.why: A compact step strip reminds students of the method they will use in every practice question.
